deck: all::LIBERTY::LIBERTY FALL 2026::BIOL 313 - Clinical Human Anatomy::Exam 1::Heart::Cardiac Cycle & Output
front: Heart sounds are turbulence from valves slamming shut. The first sound, S1 'lubb', is the sound of {{c1::AV valve}} closure, and the second, S2 'dupp', is the sound of {{c1::semilunar valve}} closure.
back_extra: Lubb marks the start of ventricular systole, when rising ventricular pressure slams the tricuspid and bicuspid shut; dupp marks its end, when blood falling back onto the aortic and pulmonary cusps snaps them closed.

front:
Inside the left ventricle:

the conical cavity turns blood through {{c1::180°::angle}}

{{c1::two::number}} papillary muscles hold the valve cusps by their cords

the smooth outflow channel to the aortic orifice is the {{c1::aortic vestibule}}

the valve at the left AV orifice is the {{c1::bicuspid (mitral)}} valve
back_extra: Blood comes in past the bicuspid valve, makes a U-turn at the apex and leaves up the aortic vestibule through the aortic valve; the two papillary muscles are the anterior and posterior ones, versus three on the right.
